storyboards: Role → STS session → S3 policy → approved report; compare IAM role ARN with assumed-role session ARN; same-account Principal:* plus PrincipalArn nuance; condition alone grants nothing.
Resource access is not role assumption

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 30. Title 'Resource access is not role assumption'. Premise 'Choose which identity makes the final S3 request.' Two architecture lanes, not generic cards. Lane A label 'Direct cross-account access': 'Account A: AppRole' -> cyan arrow 's3:GetObject' crossing account boundary -> 'Account B: S3 bucket'. Annotate 'Caller remains AppRole in Account A'; underneath compact two checks 'A identity policy allows the read' and 'B bucket policy trusts AppRole'. Lane B 'Assume a role first': 'Account A: AppRole' -> 'STS: AssumeRole' -> 'Account B: ReaderRole session' -> 'Account B: S3 bucket'. Annotate two separate gates: 'Assumption: caller permission + role trust policy'; 'Read: permissions of ReaderRole session'. Mini table at bottom 'Question | Direct | Assume role'; 'Who reads? | Account A AppRole | Account B ReaderRole session'; 'Needs sts:AssumeRole? | No | Yes'. Brief final note 'The original caller permissions do not carry into the new role session. Applicable denies and other controls still apply.' Use AWS service pictograms faithful identity, STS and green S3. No code or fabricated policies.

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 31. Title 'Authorize the EventBridge target'. Premise 'Matching an event does not grant permission to deliver it.' Scope explicit 'EventBridge event-bus rule → SQS; resource-policy example'. Upper mechanism 'Application event' -> 'Event bus' -> 'Matching rule: finance-alerts' -> 'SQS: security-events' with arrows named 'PutEvents', 'Rule match', 'sqs:SendMessage'. At SQS queue policy checkpoint list exactly 'Principal: events.amazonaws.com', 'Action: sqs:SendMessage', 'Resource: target queue ARN', 'aws:SourceArn = approved rule ARN'. Lower half diagnostic table 'Evidence | Check | Verify'; 'Rule matches, delivery fails | Target permission and ARN conditions | Send a matching test event'; 'Customer managed KMS key | Required key-policy permissions | Verify encrypted delivery'; 'Delivery failure remains | Retry/DLQ configuration | Inspect the failure reason'. Small note 'Targets can use execution roles or resource policies where supported; this example uses a queue policy.' Keep distinction between publishing permission and target delivery clear; do not claim Lambda/SQS can only use resource policies. Glossy proper colored EventBridge pink bus icon and SQS pink queue glyph, no empty squares.
Let only your S3 bucket notify SQS

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 32. Title 'Let only your S3 bucket notify SQS'. Premise 'S3 sends the notification; a separate consumer reads the queue.' Large architecture with explicit boundaries: 'S3: finance-uploads' -> arrow 'sqs:SendMessage' -> queue-policy checkpoint -> 'SQS standard queue' -> 'Consumer'. Left small event example 'ObjectCreated: reports/june.csv'. Permission checkpoint block exact conceptual fields 'Principal: s3.amazonaws.com', 'Action: sqs:SendMessage', 'SourceArn: approved bucket ARN', 'SourceAccount: bucket owner account'. Under consumer arrow label 'sqs:ReceiveMessage + sqs:DeleteMessage' and 'Consumer role permissions'. Bottom left mini outcome table 'Approved bucket + owner | ACCEPT'; 'Different bucket | DENY'; 'Wrong source account | DENY'. Bottom right operational checks 'Queue and bucket: same Region'; 'SSE-KMS queue: allow S3 required key use'; 'Direct S3 notifications do not support FIFO queues'. Add short note 'Source conditions constrain the sending service; they do not authorize the consumer.' Service icons green S3 and pink SQS, readable and appropriate.
Delegate IAM without handing over the boundary

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 33. Title 'Delegate IAM without handing over the boundary'. Premise 'Let a team create workload roles inside a protected permissions ceiling.' Architecture upper: 'Platform administrator' -> 'Approved permissions boundary' fixed protected shield; 'Team administrator' -> 'Create workload role' -> 'Workload role + approved boundary' -> 'Approved S3 access'. The creation checkpoint label 'Require iam:PermissionsBoundary on CreateRole'. Branch red blocked arrows from team admin to 'Remove boundary' and 'Change approved boundary policy'. Lower left compact diagram 'Identity policy ALLOW' intersect 'Boundary ALLOW' -> 'Identity-based effective permissions'; clearly label 'Boundary grants no permissions'. Lower right three action controls 'Restrict role and policy paths'; 'Restrict iam:PassRole and role trust'; 'Protect boundary removal and policy-version changes'. Bottom small meaningful scope note 'For identity-based grants; resource-policy grants require separate review. Explicit denies still apply.' Colorful modest IAM red identity icons and S3 green pictogram, complete arrows and no faux JSON. No claim boundary universally constrains all resource-based grants.
Use Access Analyzer for the right question

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 34. Title 'Use Access Analyzer for the right question'. Premise 'Review policy quality, reachable access and unused permissions with different checks.' Composition a four-row operational matrix with unique small colorful icons on left and flow into shared 'Review → narrow → test → monitor' ribbon below. Columns 'Question | Capability | What to do'. Row1 'Is the policy well formed? | Policy validation | Fix errors and security warnings'. Row2 'Who outside my trust zone can access it? | External access analyzer | Inspect principal and conditions'. Row3 'Which permissions were not used? | Unused access analyzer | Review before removing access'. Row4 'Does this edit add access? | Custom policy checks | Compare with a reference policy'. Above matrix mini architecture 'Resource policy' -> 'Analyzer' -> 'Finding + policy statement' with magnifier/shield icon. Right bottom worked example 'Unexpected external account' -> 'Inspect intended sharing' -> 'Narrow principal or conditions' -> 'Retest'. Useful caveat bottom 'A finding describes access; it does not prove exploitation. Findings do not change the policy automatically.' Do not promise all service resources supported, do not claim unused means never needed. Fine panels, readable text with rich cyan, purple and amber. Avoid massive title or empty space.
Checkpoint: explain the denied report read

MODULE 01 | SLIDE 35. Title 'Checkpoint: explain the denied report read'. Premise 'Trace the caller, the route, the S3 permission and the encryption key.' Upper real architecture 'Account A: ReportReader role' -> 'Approved S3 VPC endpoint' -> 'Account B: SSE-KMS report object'; branch S3 -> 'Account B: customer managed KMS key'. Evidence checklist under diagram: 'Endpoint condition matches ✓'; 'Caller IAM allows s3:GetObject ✓'; 'Bucket policy allows ReportReader ✓'; 'Caller IAM allows kms:Decrypt ✓'; 'KMS key policy does not allow ReportReader ✕'. Lower left panel label 'Before revealing the answer' and questions '1. Which authorization check fails?'; '2. What is the narrowest correction?'; '3. How will you verify it?'. Lower right visually distinct panel 'Worked resolution' with 'Failing gate: cross-account KMS authorization'; 'Allow the approved external role to decrypt with this key'; 'Retest the intended read and an unauthorized role'. Final short strip 'A private route and S3 permission do not replace KMS authorization.' Scope 'Illustrative case: all other required controls permit the request.' Keep answer separated from questions, rich modest AWS EC2 identity S3 KMS official-style colored pictograms, accurate return arrow object -> caller, no claim network endpoint directly grants authorization.
